key_insight: EpNet learns empirical pseudopotentials to predict complete crystal band structures directly from atomic coordinates across 63 s-, p-, and d-block elements.
engineering_relevance: Electronic-property screening at about 1% of DFT cost could accelerate materials discovery and enable electronic-structure simulations of larger systems.
method: Use an equivariant neural network to construct a Hamiltonian from local potentials and nonlocal projectors.
Train solely on band energies rather than Hamiltonian labels.
Predict band structures without DFT self-consistent iterations.
evidence_signal: On 600,000 structures from an independent database, the abstract reports overall band-gap errors less than half those of existing models.
watch_item: Exact median band-energy and band-gap errors are unresolved placeholders in the abstract, limiting assessment of absolute accuracy.
paper_title: Learning Electronic Band Structures Across the s, p, d Blocks with an Empirical Pseudopotential Network
